body: In 1935, Schrödinger imagined a cat sealed in a box.
A radioactive atom could trigger poison if it decayed.
Quantum theory can represent decay and no decay together.
That leaves the cat seemingly alive and dead together.
It was a challenge, not a real experiment.
Could superposition sensibly scale to everyday objects?
The paradox asks when possibilities become one ordinary outcome.
optional_closing: That is the point of the cat.
